ct-southington-fema-safer-grant-12-firef.excerpt: The FEMA award could add 12 firefighters and expand around-the-clock coverage, but the Town Council must still accept the grant and decide how to pay for the positions after federal support ends.
ct-southington-fema-safer-grant-12-firef.text: southington fire department wins $3.03 million staffing grant, but town approval is still pending the fema award could add 12 firefighters and expand around-the-clock coverage, but the town council must still accept the grant and decide how to pay for the positions after federal support ends. southington’s fire department has been awarded a $3.03 million federal grant that could add 12 firefighters to the department, a potentially significant change for a town that has relied on a mix of career staff, volunteers and mutual aid from neighboring communities. the award was announced by the department in late september and reported locally this week, but it is not yet a hiring authorization: the town council must review and accept the grant before the plan can move forward. the money comes through the federal emergency management agency’s staffing for adequate fire and emergency response program, commonly called safer. fema describes safer as a competitive grant program intended to help fire departments increase the number of firefighters, meet minimum staffing standards and achieve 24-hour coverage. its guidance says hiring awards can support the traditional missions of fire departments as well as stronger protection from fire and related hazards. [fema’s safer program guidance](https://www.fema.gov/sites/default/files/documents/fema_gpd-fy-2023-safer-faqs.pdf) provides that broader context. southington officials and department representatives say the local award would address a long-running staffing problem. the southington outsider reported that the department’s volunteer ranks have fallen from more than 100 people about 14 years ago to roughly 20 now, according to captain daniel comen, who wrote the grant application. that decline has left the station at 35 clark street staffed only on weekdays, the publication reported. the new grant is intended to make that station available around the clock. the operational goal is more than adding names to a roster. comen told the southington outsider that the department now has as many as seven firefighters on duty and can fall to six, while the grant-supported plan would raise the regular daily level to 11, with a low point of 10. the department says that additional coverage could make it easier to send a crew to an emergency without leaving another station short-handed. the department also expects the staffing change to reduce its dependence on neighboring towns for routine coverage. southington currently calls on mutual-aid partners in meriden, bristol, new britain, plainville and cheshire when it needs to maintain station coverage while responding to a larger fire, according to comen’s account in the southington outsider. he said the department’s goal is to reduce routine mutual-aid requests by about half. that is a department target, not a guaranteed result of the award, and actual response times will depend on hiring, training, scheduling and call volume. the award is unusually large by the department’s accounting. southington fire department officials told patch that it was the only fiscal-year 2025 safer award announced for a connecticut department at the time, the largest announced in new england, the second-largest in the northeast and the 11th-largest nationally. those rankings are based on awards announced so far, rather than a permanent ranking of every fire department or a measure of fire outcomes. the quinnipiac post reported the same pending-review status and described the award as one of the largest in the region based on the department’s figures. the unresolved issue is what happens after the federal grant period. patch reported that the award would offset the cost of hiring the 12 firefighters, but that local officials and taxpayers would ultimately have to decide whether to keep funding the positions when federal money runs out. the southington outsider also reported that the department expects the added staffing to reduce overtime costs, but potential savings do not by themselves establish the town’s future payroll obligation. the town has not yet announced a final implementation schedule or long-term cost decision. the next formal checkpoint is the town council’s review and acceptance of the grant. patch reported that the council’s next regular meeting is scheduled for oct. 12 at the john weichsel municipal center, while the southington outsider reported that the department expected the grant to be considered at a meeting on oct. 13. the differing dates show why the agenda and the council’s official action should be checked before treating the award as final. until the council acts, southington has a federal staffing opportunity, not 12 newly hired firefighters. connecticut public-safety public safety ct southington southington, connecticut connecticut southington firefighters ct-suffield-school-bus-crash-2026-10-01.text: suffield school bus crash sends 11 to hospitals with minor injuries a region 12 bus carrying students left south grand street and struck a building thursday morning; police said the cause remains under investigation. eleven people were taken to two local hospitals with minor injuries thursday after a small school bus carrying students left the roadway and struck a building in suffield, connecticut. the crash brought police, fire and ambulance crews to south grand street and left investigators working to determine why the bus veered off the road. suffield police said officers responded to the area of 425 south grand st. at about 9:49 a.m. after receiving a report of a motor-vehicle crash with possible injuries. their preliminary account said the bus was traveling north toward mountain road when it left the right shoulder and collided with a building beside the street. police did not announce a mechanical problem, medical event, weather factor or other cause. the bus came from regional school district 12, which serves communities in the shepaug valley. nbc connecticut reported that students were aboard, while the suffield volunteer ambulance association said 15 people, including the driver, were on the small bus. the association said 10 students and the driver were transported for evaluation. authorities did not release the students’ ages or identify the hospitals. the ambulance response required help from several nearby agencies. the ambulance association said it sent three ambulances staffed by paramedics, while enfield ems and the windsor locks lions club ambulance provided additional units. north central cmed helped coordinate the transports and contacted receiving hospitals to confirm that they could accommodate the patients. that coordination also shaped how the students were handled after the crash. according to the ambulance association’s statement reported by patch, responders tried to keep the students together when possible so school staff and families could receive information more easily. region 12 personnel came to the scene to assist the students, and emergency officials said the response was managed through the area’s normal mutual-aid system. the ambulance association also pushed back on online descriptions of the incident as a mass-casualty or multi-casualty event. it said the scene required significant coordination but did not meet that designation. that distinction describes the emergency-management classification, not the seriousness of the reported injuries: police and ambulance officials said everyone taken for treatment had minor injuries. hearst connecticut media reported that the bus was carrying shepaug valley school students on the way to a fair and that a region 12 official said the vehicle was driven by a properly licensed teacher. that account adds context to the trip but does not resolve the central unanswered question of what caused the bus to leave south grand street. police interviewed people involved and said the investigation was continuing. south grand street was closed while the scene was investigated and later reopened, according to local reports. no charges or citations had been announced in the available accounts. for families and residents, the immediate outcome was that the 11 people transported for care had reported minor ct-tv-to-table-trail-launch-2026-10-06.excerpt: The new tourism guide highlights more than 60 Connecticut restaurants and chefs featured on national food programs, with a Stamford launch hosted by Waterbury native Scott Conant.
ct-tv-to-table-trail-launch-2026-10-06.text: connecticut launches tv-to-table trail linking food-show fame to local restaurants the new tourism guide highlights more than 60 connecticut restaurants and chefs featured on national food programs, with a stamford launch hosted by waterbury native scott conant. connecticut has turned its television food cameos into a statewide tourism itinerary. gov. ned lamont and the connecticut office of statewide marketing and tourism announced the launch of the [connecticut tv-to-table trail](https://portal.ct.gov/governor/news/press-releases/2026/10-2026/governor-lamont-announces-tv-to-table-trail) on oct. 5, inviting visitors to go from watching a chef or restaurant on screen to visiting the place where the food is made. the program is built as a promotional guide rather than a single road route. the state’s [ctvisit directory](https://ctvisit.com/articles/connecticut-tv-table-trail) presents the trail as a map of restaurants and food destinations that have appeared on television, giving travelers a way to search for stops across connecticut. the launch announcement says the featured businesses include chefs who have appeared on chopped, beat bobby flay, diners, drive-ins and dives, best bite in town, guy’s grocery games and cupcake wars. the breadth is part of the pitch. the [hour reported](https://www3.thehour.com/food/article/connecticut-tv-table-trail-22454768.php) before the launch that more than 60 eateries were included, spread across fairfield, hartford, new haven, new london, tolland and other connecticut counties. the list ranges from greenwich restaurants such as colony grill and corbo’s southside deli to bridgeport’s merritt canteen, fairfield’s rawley’s drive-in and new haven’s da legna x
